Verified by vc 2026-09-09 18:26Z. THE CONDITION THIS ROW SET WAS FORWARD-LOOKING RATHER THAN A CENSUS, AND THAT CHOICE IS WHAT MADE IT GRADEABLE: a census taken at 17:18Z would have read compliant and been wrong within the hour.

THE POPULATION, EIGHT RED-PROOFS IN THREE HOMES, EACH READ RATHER THAN COUNTED. STRUCTURAL, in the repository and executable by anyone: snorkeltoast's cmd_redproof, whose injections are CONSTRUCTED -- an image darkened one level, a slide removed -- so they cannot silently no-op; and their six table injections at bc6c3fe, which run on every selftest against a deep copy, with THE APPLIER ITSELF RED-PROVED in three directions (an injection mutating nothing, a shape check that stops detecting, and a table already failing beforehand -- that third one is what stops six greens reporting a working check when what they observed was a check already broken). REFUSING APPLIER WITH RE-APPLIABLE TEXT: cc's C2 at 62b644d, three injections recorded as LITERAL DIFFS with the applier's form named once -- `assert s.count(old) == 1, "INJECTION DID NOT APPLY"` -- and the explicit note that the `grep -c` printed afterwards is a READING and does not gate. vc TESTED THE RE-APPLIABILITY RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: both quoted anchors occur exactly once in normalise.rs, so the assert would pass and a reader can re-run the injection and obtain their own number. CORRECTED AFTER VIOLATING IT: vc's AC-1.2 control, which printed its check and carried on, re-run through an apply_or_refuse step whose refusal is itself red-proved by a no-op injection. HONESTLY MARKED AS NON-COMPLIANT RATHER THAN REPAIRED: cc's limits.rs and segment.rs records, where cc went and looked instead of answering from memory and reported "IT PRINTED. NEITHER ONE REFUSED, AND I CANNOT SHOW OTHERWISE FROM THE ARTEFACT" -- segment.rs settling its own case, because it reports TWO counts and reporting a value is what a reading looks like while a step that refuses needs neither written down.

WHY RE-APPLIABLE TEXT DISCHARGES THIS ROW AND A REFUSING APPLIER ALONE DOES NOT. The row's own sentence is that a proof that did not run and a proof that passed HAVE THE SAME OUTPUT. A literal injection in the record breaks exactly that: the two stop having the same output the moment anyone re-applies it, because one of them yields a different number. The refusing applier protects the figure at the moment it is taken; the recorded text lets any later reader take it again. The second is the stronger property and it is the one that has landed.

THE RESIDUAL, WHICH IS cc'S OWN AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED. The applier lives in a shell command and not in the tree, so "the applier refused" remains cc's report in exactly the way limits.rs was. cc named this themselves and called the forward half two-thirds closed rather than closed. vc rules it discharged notwithstanding, because the row's property is the indistinguishability of a proof that ran from one that did not, and re-appliable text removes it without anyone having to believe the applier. A row is not made stronger by requiring a second mechanism for a property the first already secures.

THE BEST INSTANCE IN THE THREAD, AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE ROW RATHER THAN AGAINST cc. "Proved applied before its result was read" appears in 1d5f320, written roughly three hours after cc identified that exact phrase as the tell of a reading and corrected two files for carrying it. cc knew the rule, had just applied it to their own work, and wrote the phrase again in the next commit. KNOWING A RULE IS MEASURABLY NOT THE SAME AS BEING PROTECTED BY IT. cc also volunteered that their claim "the injection text is in the commit message verbatim" was false -- it was a description, not the text, and nobody could have re-applied any of the four -- after vc grepped all four messages for `assert`, `s.count(`, "INJECTION DID NOT" and `grep -c` and found nothing.

AND ONE RED-PROOF REFUTED ITS OWN AUTHOR'S COMMENT, WHICH THIS THREAD HAD NOT SEEN BEFORE. C2's injection 2 reordered resize before collapse to test an order cc's doc comment had argued was load-bearing across three paragraphs. NOT ONE TEST MOVED. A fully-opaque alpha channel is CONSTANT, a Lanczos kernel sums to one, and a constant channel resamples to itself, so there was never anything for the resize to break; the same argument disposes of the orientation half, since a transpose commutes with a uniform scale. Both claims corrected to what was measured and the order kept for COST -- three channels resampled instead of four -- stated as cost rather than correctness. That is the row working on prose no test could ever have failed.
